seams.description: LogWriter ↔ rotation module: __init__ and append() trigger points in app/logger.py call rotate() then apply_retention() in app/rotation.py. Consistency risks: wrong argument (live file vs its parent dir), hook placed after the write instead of before, missing apply_retention call, import cycle (rotation importing logger), timestamp-parse vs mtime-fallback disagreement between writer and module.

LogWriter ↔ consumers (serve loop + pre-existing tests): the C2 public interface must stay byte-compatible so app/server.py and tests/test_log.py run unmodified. Consistency risks: append() signature or per-line behavior drift, live file path/naming change breaking the server's 'logs/app.log' reference.

omitted_kinds.reason: A separate read-only diff pass would duplicate what the two small leaves already assert against the frozen specs: T01's unit tests execute C1/C3 signatures and semantics line-by-line, T02's wiring tests execute C2, and T03 re-asserts the observable contract surface (A5 runs the unmodified pre-existing suite; A6 asserts the C3 file layout end-to-end) — for a 2-leaf alpha plan a fourth task adds no independent check.
evidence: A5: python -m unittest tests.test_log -v passes unmodified (C2 surface)
A6: e2e asserts app-YYYYMMDD.log / .gz layout per C3
T01 outputs tests/test_rotation.py asserting C1/C3 behavior
T02 outputs tests/test_log_rotation.py asserting C1 hook wiring per C2

e2e_gates.scenario: Happy-path midnight crossing through serve(): clock pinned at 23:59:50, 23:59:59, 00:00:01 on consecutive ticks — first two lines end up in app-<day1>.log, third in app.log, total line count preserved, and the retention pass ran after the rotation (oldest rotated file deleted when 8+ existed beforehand).

Restart failure scenario (S1): process restarts mid-history with a stale live log (last line dated before today); LogWriter construction rotates the stale file before any append, then same-day appends stay in the fresh live file; no line lost across the restart.

Bad-input failure scenario (S1): live log's last line has no parseable timestamp (corrupt line); rotation falls back to the mtime date per C1, append still succeeds, no crash, no line lost, and the corrupt file is archived whole (not truncated or dropped).

Existing-consumer failure scenario (S2): the pre-existing test suite runs unmodified and green, and tests/test_log.py is byte-identical to the snapshot revision — any failure or diff means the C2 seam broke in T02.
